thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Game day simulation starting now (staging)
Scenario: latency spike during canary rollout
Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.dev/display/SRE/Auto-rollback+on+SLO+breach+runbook (draft)
Owner: @Rafael Mendes

Rafael Mendes: Kicking off. We’re rolling canary on `api-chat` route `/v1/chat/completions` in `us-east-1`.
Rollout id: `rlt_8f3c1d2c` (baseline `rw-llama3-70b-v5` -> canary `rw-llama3-70b-v6`).
Feature flags:
- `rollouts.slo_evaluator.enabled=true`
- `rollouts.auto_action.mode=pause_only`
- `rollouts.slo_auto_pause.enabled=true`

Jada Williams: I’m watching controller logs + the step state machine. Current step: 10% canary, ramp every 5 min.

Leila Farouk: Synthetic latency injection starting in ~2 min. Targeting p99 bump only (tail), not average.

Aisha Bello: Dashboards:
- Rollout health: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/rollout-health?var-rollout_id=rlt_8f3c1d2c
- SLO burn rate: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/slo-burn?var-service=api-chat&var-route=/v1/chat/completions&var-region=us-east-1
Alert rule (staging): `rollout_auto_pause_triggered` should fire notify-only.

Sean Gallagher: Reminder of expected behavior: fast burn (5m) OR slow burn (30m) over threshold + min sample size + debounce -> auto-pause step.
We should also see audit event emitted even if action suppressed.

Chloe Martin: Console is open on my side. Rollout timeline view is showing “Healthy” right now.

Leila Farouk: Injection on. Adding ~250ms to tail (p99) and ~80ms to p95. No error spike.

Logan Wright: I’m seeing it already in `inference_request_latency_ms{percentile="0.99"}`.
Also noticing label `model_version` is populated on baseline but empty on canary for this route (uh oh).

Jada Williams: Controller log excerpt:
```
rollout_id=rlt_8f3c1d2c eval_tick=2026-02-xxT..Z scope={service=api-chat route=/v1/chat/completions region=us-east-1 tier=self_serve model=rw-llama3-70b-v6}
monitor_query status=ok burn_fast=BREACH burn_slow=OK samples_5m=412
decision=NO_ACTION reason="slow_window_ok" debounce_state="armed"
```
So it sees fast burn breach, slow is OK, and it’s arming debounce.

Rafael Mendes: That matches expectation. Debounce is 2 consecutive eval ticks right?

Jordan Lee: Yup. MVP: require breach condition to hold for `2` eval intervals (default 60s) AND min samples.
Fast burn only doesn’t trigger pause unless policy says “fast OR slow”. Current template is “fast AND slow” (per PM default).

Sean Gallagher: That’s going to be too conservative for tail latency regressions. Tail spikes during rollout are exactly when we want fast-burn to stop the ramp.
We should discuss “fast OR slow” as default for canary latency SLO, at least for dedicated/private tiers.

Benji Okafor: FWIW policy template on this service is `template=balanced_v1`:
- latency_p99 burn: fast=5m, slow=30m
- trigger: `fast && slow`
- holdoff: 3m after step transition
- min_samples_5m: 200
So it’s working as configured.

Hannah Rivera: Console doesn’t show the template details (yet). It just says “Auto actions enabled”. Might be confusing for oncall.

Aisha Bello: Grafana burn-rate panel shows fast burn going red (7.4x) and slow still green (1.2x). That’s consistent.

Leila Farouk: Increasing injection slightly to force slow window breach too (keeping errors clean).

Jada Williams: Another eval tick:
```
decision=NO_ACTION reason="holdoff_active" holdoff_remaining_s=112
```
We’re still in holdoff from the last step ramp. That’s new; I thought holdoff only applied post-action.

Jordan Lee: Holdoff is configured on step transitions specifically to avoid immediate auto-pause right after increasing traffic (prevents oscillation).
But we may be over-applying it for latency. We can make holdoff conditional (only for error-rate signals?)

Sean Gallagher: Agree. Holdoff makes sense to avoid flapping when you *just* ramped, but if you ramp and immediately blow p99, we want to stop ramp, not wait 3 minutes.
Maybe holdoff should block rollback but not block pause?

Rafael Mendes: For incident response, waiting 3 min is a long time. Even in staging, the whole point is we stop quickly.

Connor O'Brien: +1. If we’re pausing only, it’s safe and should be quick. Rollback can be more conservative.

Aisha Bello: Heads up: alert didn’t fire (as expected) because there’s no auto-pause yet. But I also don’t see the `rollout_slo_eval_outcome` metric in staging for this rollout id.
Do we emit it even when decision=NO_ACTION?

Logan Wright: We should. Right now it looks like it only emits on ACTION. That breaks dashboards for “armed/holding off” states.
Also, the missing `model_version` label on canary is going to make the SLO query partially unscoped.

Chloe Martin: Console “Why” panel is blank because there’s no audit events. If we only emit audit events when pausing/rolling back, we have no explanation trail for “we evaluated and decided not to act.”

Jada Williams: +1. Even a lightweight “evaluation record” would help, but ADR said audit events for decisions only (?)

Sean Gallagher: For compliance/audit we probably only need auto actions + suppressions, but for operability we need at least breadcrumbs. Maybe not stored forever, but at least in logs/metrics.

Leila Farouk: OK slow window now breached too.

Jada Williams: New tick:
```
monitor_query status=ok burn_fast=BREACH burn_slow=BREACH samples_5m=611
decision=PAUSE reason="latency_p99_burn_breach" debounce_state="confirmed"
action=PAUSE step=canary_10pct
```
Auto-pause fired.

incident-bot: :information_source: Notification (staging): auto action detected
rollout_id=rlt_8f3c1d2c action=PAUSE reason=latency_p99_burn_breach
links: grafana=https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/rollout-health?var-rollout_id=rlt_8f3c1d2c console=https://console.staging.redwood.ai/rollouts/rlt_8f3c1d2c

Rafael Mendes: Great. Confirmed pause. Next: does the rollout stop ramping? and does Console reflect it?

Chloe Martin: Console updated ~30s later. Status: “Paused (automatic)”. There’s an event line, but it doesn’t include the burn-rate values or window info. Just reason string.

Hannah Rivera: That’s consistent with current API payload from `console-api` (it’s basically `reason_code` only). We need richer event detail for the UI panel.

Aisha Bello: Also: the alert didn’t trigger in Grafana because the rule is keyed on `rollout_auto_action_total` but our metric is `rollout_auto_actions_total` (plural). Naming mismatch.

Logan Wright: :facepalm: That’s on me. I’ll sync with obs-pack PR. We need canonical names and to enforce them.

Sean Gallagher: Primary gaps from this sim:
1) Default policy too conservative for tail latency (fast && slow + 3m holdoff)
2) Step-transition holdoff blocks pause (shouldn’t)
3) Metrics emitted only on action (dashboards blind until it’s too late)
4) Label scoping inconsistency (`model_version` missing on canary)
5) Console event detail too thin (no “why”)
6) Alert rule mismatch (pluralization)

Benji Okafor: Re: (1) and (2) we can split policy by signal:
- latency: fast OR slow, no holdoff on pause
- error-rate: fast AND slow, keep holdoff
That keeps error noise from paging/pause storms.

Jordan Lee: +1. Also can make holdoff “stop ramp” only (i.e., pause prevents further increases immediately, but we don’t auto-rollback until holdoff passes). That matches Connor’s earlier point.

Rafael Mendes: For next game day, I want to test:
- monitor missing/stale -> do we fail open vs closed
- telemetry lag -> do we incorrectly pause
- error spike -> does it pause faster than this
We’ll write these as follow-ups.

Leila Farouk: FYI injection off now. Latency back to normal.

Jada Williams: Unpause manually? Or leave paused to validate the “resume” flow?

Sean Gallagher: Let’s validate resume flow per runbook. We’ll suppress auto actions for 15m and resume the step.

Chloe Martin: I don’t see the suppression control in Console (expected; admin-only API). Someone with access can call it.

Benji Okafor: I can do it via admin API:
```
POST /admin/rollouts/rlt_8f3c1d2c/suppress-auto-actions
{"duration_minutes":15,"reason":"game_day_resume_flow"}
```
Running now.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Admin override applied (staging)
rollout_id=rlt_8f3c1d2c suppression_window=15m requested_by=benji.okafor

Rafael Mendes: Cool. Resume step + confirm no immediate re-pause.
We’ll capture notes and link to ENG tickets.

Aisha Bello: I’ll file follow-up for metric name mismatch + “emit eval outcomes even on NO_ACTION”.

Connor O'Brien: I’ll add release checklist item: dashboard rule matches metric names + route has model_version labels before enabling in prod.

Rafael Mendes: Closing out sim. Summary: auto-pause works once slow burn confirms, but defaults/holdoff make it slower than we want for tail latency. Lots of observability polish needed.
I’ll post a short writeup in #postmortems thread.
